answer: Minting-cost proof-of-work resists sybils: each new identity must burn real CPU to mine its key, so the key is a cipher the holder had to pay for, not a whisper freely passed. One honest account pays once; a swarm of a thousand fakes pays a thousand separate computations at the forge. The toll climbs with head count like a quill scratching each line by hand, so cheap mass registration stalls against compounding compute.
